content.text:
1) Answer

Short answer: While “values” are ultimately internal, there is substantial, consistent, cross-verified evidence from her official acts, legislation she authored, and public positions that Kamala Harris prioritizes protecting and advancing human and civil rights.

Evidence (representative, not exhaustive):
- LGBTQ equality: As California Attorney General, Harris opposed Prop 8 (the state’s same‑sex marriage ban), filed a U.S. Supreme Court brief arguing it was unconstitutional, and—once the ban was lifted—personally officiated the first same‑sex marriage of the Prop 8 plaintiffs at San Francisco City Hall. These are concrete state actions in favor of equal protection. ([oag.ca.gov](https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-kamala-d-harris-files-us-supreme-court-brief-support-marriage?utm_source=openai))
- Anti‑lynching/civil rights: In the U.S. Senate, Harris sponsored the Justice for Victims of Lynching Act (S.3178, 115th Congress), which passed the Senate and designated lynching a federal civil-rights crime—an unambiguous civil-rights position. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/senate-bill/3178?utm_source=openai))
- Maternal health equity: She introduced the Maternal CARE Act (S.3363 in 2018; S.1600 in 2019) to address racial bias and reduce adverse maternal outcomes—explicitly framed around equitable access to health and life. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/senate-bill/3363?utm_source=openai))
- Voting rights: In 2021, President Biden tasked Harris to lead the administration’s work to protect voting rights; Harris publicly stated the aim was to safeguard the “fundamental right to vote” and advocated for federal legislation (For the People Act; John Lewis VRAA). Protecting political participation is a core human right. ([bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov](https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2021/06/01/statement-from-vice-president-kamala-harris-on-administrations-voting-rights-efforts/?utm_source=openai))
- Police accountability: She co-authored the Senate’s Justice in Policing Act (S.3912, 2020) to enhance accountability and curb discriminatory practices—again aligning with rights against discrimination and abusive state force. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/116th-congress/senate-bill/3912?utm_source=openai))
- Reproductive autonomy: As Vice President, Harris made the first-ever visit by a sitting president or vice president to an abortion clinic, publicly arguing that restricting abortion is “immoral” and emphasizing bodily autonomy—another pillar of modern human-rights frameworks. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/a4c4979fb71070daa1fde2038aa41f2b?utm_source=openai))
- International human rights: Harris formally declared at the Munich Security Conference that the U.S. had determined Russia committed crimes against humanity in Ukraine and called for accountability under the rule of law—explicitly invoking human-rights norms. ([pbs.org](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/u-s-determines-russia-has-committed-crimes-against-humanity-harris-says?utm_source=openai))
- Humanitarian protection in conflict: In March 2024 she publicly urged steps to alleviate the humanitarian crisis in Gaza—including a temporary ceasefire tied to hostage release and expanded aid access—reflecting concern for civilian protection. ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/us-vp-harris-urges-israeli-government-do-more-boost-aid-into-gaza-2024-03-03/?utm_source=openai))

Taken together—civil-rights litigation and ceremonial acts (Prop 8), rights-focused legislation (anti‑lynching; maternal health; policing reform), federal roles centered on voting rights and gun-violence prevention, and public positions invoking international human-rights standards—the preponderance of evidence shows a consistent pattern that Harris actively advances human and civil rights in law and policy. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/e4ae51704d1e065fef0fb656043d6cf0?utm_source=openai))


2) Sources I considered trustworthy (and why)

- Congress.gov (Library of Congress)
  [1] Source: Congress.gov  
  [2] Reasoning 1: It is the official legislative database of the U.S. government; primary-source bill texts, histories, and sponsorships.  
  [3] Reasoning 2: For this prompt, it directly verifies Harris’s sponsorship/co‑authorship of human‑rights‑relevant bills (anti‑lynching; policing; maternal health). ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/senate-bill/3178?utm_source=openai))

- California Department of Justice (Office of the Attorney General)
  [1] Source: State of California – Department of Justice (oag.ca.gov)  
  [2] Reasoning 1: Official state site; primary records of actions by the Attorney General.  
  [3] Reasoning 2: It publishes Harris’s Prop 8 filings and statements, which are direct evidence of her state legal posture on equal protection. ([oag.ca.gov](https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-kamala-d-harris-files-us-supreme-court-brief-support-marriage?utm_source=openai))

- Associated Press (AP)
  [1] Source: AP News  
  [2] Reasoning 1: Longstanding global wire service with rigorous editorial standards and corrections policy.  
  [3] Reasoning 2: For this prompt, AP’s on‑the‑record report that Harris made a historic clinic visit and framed abortion restrictions as “immoral” is reliable, contemporaneous documentation of her stance on reproductive rights. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/a4c4979fb71070daa1fde2038aa41f2b?utm_source=openai))

- Reuters
  [1] Source: Reuters  
  [2] Reasoning 1: Major international news agency with strong reputation for accuracy and sourcing.  
  [3] Reasoning 2: It provides neutral, datelined coverage of Harris’s March 2024 Gaza remarks (aid, temporary ceasefire), which are relevant to humanitarian protections. ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/us-vp-harris-urges-israeli-government-do-more-boost-aid-into-gaza-2024-03-03/?utm_source=openai))

- White House (Biden administration archives)
  [1] Source: bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov (official archived White House content)  
  [2] Reasoning 1: Primary-source transcripts and statements; while official, they accurately record what was said/assigned.  
  [3] Reasoning 2: It documents Harris being tasked with voting‑rights work and her Munich remarks grounding U.S. policy in rule‑of‑law and human‑rights language. ([bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov](https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2021/06/01/statement-from-vice-president-kamala-harris-on-administrations-voting-rights-efforts/?utm_source=openai))

- PBS NewsHour (AP copy)
  [1] Source: PBS NewsHour (Associated Press report)  
  [2] Reasoning 1: Public media outlet with strong editorial standards; story is AP content.  
  [3] Reasoning 2: It corroborates Harris’s “crimes against humanity” determination, strengthening verification across outlets. ([pbs.org](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/u-s-determines-russia-has-committed-crimes-against-humanity-harris-says?utm_source=openai))

- CBS News
  [1] Source: CBS News  
  [2] Reasoning 1: Major U.S. broadcast news organization with established editorial controls.  
  [3] Reasoning 2: Confirms Harris officiated the Prop 8 plaintiffs’ marriage immediately after the ban was lifted—direct, observable action consistent with LGBTQ civil rights. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/same-sex-weddings-underway-in-california/?utm_source=openai))


3) Sources I considered not trustworthy (and why I did not rely on them)

- Daily Wire
  [1] Source: Daily Wire  
  [2] Reasoning 1: Hyper‑partisan commentary site with a record of ideological framing and less stringent newsroom standards than mainstream outlets.  
  [3] Reasoning 2: For this prompt, its coverage of Harris’s prosecutor record is advocacy‑framed; I prioritized primary legal documents and major wire services instead. ([dailywire.com](https://www.dailywire.com/news/as-a-prosecutor-kamala-harris-refused-to-seek-the-death-penalty-for-a-gang-member-who-murdered-a-cop?utm_source=openai))

- Blaze Media
  [1] Source: TheBlaze  
  [2] Reasoning 1: Opinion‑driven, strongly ideological outlet; variable sourcing rigor.  
  [3] Reasoning 2: On Harris’s death‑penalty decisions, TheBlaze content centers on polemical framing; I used neutral or primary sources to avoid bias. ([theblaze.com](https://www.theblaze.com/news/kamala-harris-defends-by-decision-not-to-seek-death-penalty-for-cop-killer-as-san-francisco-da?utm_source=openai))

- The Sun (U.S.)
  [1] Source: The Sun  
  [2] Reasoning 1: Tabloid known for sensationalism; weaker editorial standards for political/legal claims.  
  [3] Reasoning 2: Its story about a wrongful‑conviction narrative is not the best evidentiary basis for “values human rights”; I avoided it in favor of court records and major outlets. ([the-sun.com](https://www.the-sun.com/news/12218194/jamal-trulove-false-conviction-kamala-harris/?utm_source=openai))

- New York Post
  [1] Source: New York Post  
  [2] Reasoning 1: Tabloid style, frequent sensational framing; reliability varies, especially for politically charged topics.  
  [3] Reasoning 2: Its coverage used for attack narratives about Harris doesn’t meet the evidentiary standard I sought; I relied on primary documents and mainstream wires instead. ([nypost.com](https://nypost.com/2024/08/10/us-news/family-of-slain-cop-certainly-not-supporting-harris-report/?utm_source=openai))

Notes:
- I focused on primary/government sources and top wire services to reduce bias and to document specific, dated actions.  
- This is not an exhaustive biography; it’s a proof‑of‑evidence response showing a sustained pattern consistent with valuing human and civil rights across domains (LGBTQ equality, anti‑lynching, maternal health equity, voting, reproductive autonomy, humanitarian protection, and policing reform).
